insights.claim: model-metadata-collection uses a build-time generation, runtime data-serving pattern where Go CLI tools generate catalog YAML during CI/CD, but only the static YAML files are shipped in the production container image.
insights.reasoning: The Dockerfile.konflux copies only pre-generated YAML catalog files into the image and sets CMD to sleep infinity. The Go executables (model-extractor, metadata-report) are build-time tools that are not included in the shipped image. This separation means the production container has zero attack surface from network-facing code, and catalog updates require a full image rebuild.

insights.claim: FIPS compliance is architecturally not applicable for the shipped artifact because the production container contains no executable binaries — only static YAML data files on a ubi9-minimal base.
insights.reasoning: The container ships no Go binaries, no OpenSSL, and no crypto libraries. check-payload FIPS validation for Go binaries (dynamic linking, OpenSSL presence) does not apply because no Go binaries exist in the image. The build-time Go tools use default crypto/tls but are never shipped. This is a valid architectural exception to FIPS requirements.

insights.claim: Build-time external API credentials (HF_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN) are consumed via environment variables with no rotation mechanism; compromise of CI/CD credentials would allow catalog data poisoning.
insights.reasoning: Both tokens are read from environment variables with no expiration or rotation. The tokens are optional (unauthenticated access works with rate limits), but when present they grant write access to catalog content through the CI/CD pipeline. This is mitigated by the catalog files being committed to the repository where changes are reviewable.
